Released: 04 June 2026

Version 2.0.0 is the first Hybrid Manager (HM) operator release with its own version number and its own release cadence, separate from HM.

## Highlights

- **The operator is now released independently of HM.** The operator has its own version number and its own release cadence, so you can pick up operator fixes and improvements without waiting for an HM release. A single `2.x` operator supports a range of HM versions — see the [compatibility matrix](../compatibility_matrix).

- **The `bootstrap` and `edbpgai-bootstrap` Helm charts are deprecated.** Installing HM through either chart is no longer supported. Migrate to the unified HM Helm chart.

- **Private and air-gapped registries are easier to work with.** You can trust a custom CA for `kapp-controller`, install an in-cluster container registry through the operator Helm chart, and point the operator at an HM Registry.

## Features

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Configurable <code>kapp-controller</code> TLS trust
</summary><hr/><p>You can set a custom CA certificate trust, or disable TLS verification, for private container registries. The setting is exposed both on the operator Helm chart and on the <code>HybridControlPlane</code> custom resource.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Optional in-cluster container registry
</summary><hr/><p>The operator Helm chart can now install an in-cluster container registry, which removes the need for an external registry in disconnected environments.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Support for HM Registry
</summary><hr/><p>The operator can source images from an HM Registry, and <code>HybridControlPlane</code> resources are integrated with it.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Support for pre-upgrade and post-upgrade jobs
</summary><hr/><p>You can run jobs before and after an upgrade. The upgrade job can be skipped, and it can be run more than once.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary><code>componentsParameters</code> is available during Helm chart rendering
</summary><hr/><p>Component parameters are included in the Helm chart render and expansion context, so component values can be templated from the <code>HybridControlPlane</code> resource.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Custom load balancer annotation support
</summary><hr/><p>You can set your own annotations on the load balancers the operator creates.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Support for AKS, MicroK8s, and NKP
</summary><hr/><p>The operator adds platform flavors for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), MicroK8s, and Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP), alongside the existing platforms.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Enhancements

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Managed resources are labeled <code>pgai.enterprisedb.com/system</code>
</summary><hr/><p>Every resource the operator manages carries the <code>pgai.enterprisedb.com/system</code> label, and the operator namespace is labeled as a PGAI system namespace, which makes operator-owned resources easier to identify and select.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Changes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>The operator is versioned and released independently of Hybrid Manager
</summary><hr/><p>The operator no longer shares a version number or a release cadence with HM. A single <code>2.x</code> operator supports a range of HM versions, so upgrading the operator and upgrading HM are now separate operations. Run <code>edbctl hm upgrade-operator</code> to move to the latest operator available in your registry, then set <code>spec.version</code> in your <code>HybridControlPlane</code> manifest to choose the HM version.</p>
<p>The operator also now enforces the remote method for operations, overriding any locally specified methods, so that cluster management behaves consistently.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>The portal domain is configured with <code>portal_domain_name</code>
</summary><hr/><p>The operator uses <code>portal_domain_name</code> to configure the portal domain, instead of deriving it from the <code>trust_domain</code> parameter. The trust domain is configured separately, and additional allowed trust domains can be set through the values file.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary><code>prometheus-operator</code> can be disabled when it is already installed
</summary><hr/><p>Where the target platform already provides <code>prometheus-operator</code>, the component can now be disabled outright rather than only having its CRDs annotated to avoid conflicts.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>

</details></td></tr>
